fullPassage:
Daniel Dennett argues that one benefit of having moral considerations in our conceptual repertoire is that they can serve as conversation-stoppers: their value is to bring deliberations to a close. We are rational creatures, always able to ask for justification, and this is a trait that has served us well in many contexts.

(A) This is potentially as much a problem for our own private deliberations as for our public interpersonal ones. Dennett suggests that it is useful to have "consideration-generator-squelchers": items that, once introduced, stop any further deliberation in its tracks.
(B) "That would be morally wrong!" would appear to work in this manner. Once the claim is accepted then there is no need or room for seeking further justification: the action mustn't be done, even if it is tempting, and that's all there is to it.
(C) The problem is that upon receiving a perfectly good answer we can always sensibly respond "Okay, but what justifies that?" — and we can potentially do so endlessly, never coming to a decision, forever hesitant and doubting, undone by our own rational capacity.

questions.passage: Daniel Dennett argues that one benefit of having moral considerations in our conceptual repertoire is that they can serve as conversation-stoppers: their value is to bring deliberations to a close. We are rational creatures, always able to ask for justification, and this is a trait that has served us well in many contexts. This is potentially as much a problem for our own private deliberations as for our public interpersonal ones. Dennett suggests that it is useful to have "consideration-generator-squelchers": items that, once introduced, stop any further deliberation in its tracks. "That would be morally wrong!" would appear to work in this manner. Once the claim is accepted then there is no need or room for seeking further justification: the action mustn't be done, even if it is tempting, and that's all there is to it. The problem is that upon receiving a perfectly good answer we can always sensibly respond "Okay, but what justifies that?" — and we can potentially do so endlessly, never coming to a decision, forever hesitant and doubting, undone by our own rational capacity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: Dennett은 도덕적 고려가 숙고를 끝내는(bring deliberations to a close) 역할을 한다고 봄. 시작하게 한다는 것은 불일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)에서 'as much a problem for our own private deliberations'라고 하여 일치
❌ ④ (B)에서 'the action mustn't be done'이라고 하여 일치
❌ ③ 본문에서 'this is a trait that has served us well in many contexts'라고 하여 일치
✅ ② Dennett은 도덕적 고려가 숙고를 '끝내는' 역할이라고 함. '시작하게 하는' 것은 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: their value is to bring deliberations to a close — 숙고를 끝내는 것이지 시작하는 것이 아님
